t.6.81.1: Having entered the assembly hall, the king, dejected and deeply grieved, sat down upon the foremost seat, breathing heavily like an enraged lion.
t.6.81.2: Then the mighty Rāvaṇa, worn down by grief over the calamity that had befallen his son, spoke these words to all the chiefs of his army, who stood before him with joined palms.
t.6.81.3: Let all of you sally forth, surrounded by the entire host of elephants and horses, and splendidly arrayed with throngs of chariots and with foot-soldiers.
t.6.81.4: Surrounding Rāma, who stands alone, in battle, you ought to slay him, exultant, with a shower of arrows, like clouds in the rainy season.
t.6.81.6: Thus receiving the command of the lord of the rākṣasas, those rākṣasas swiftly sallied forth in their chariots, surrounded by divisions of elephants.
t.6.81.5: Or else tomorrow, in the great battle, with you beside me, I shall slay Rāma, his limbs pierced by sharp arrows, while the whole world looks on.
t.6.81.7: Toward the rising of the sun, that most terrible and tumultuous battle took place between the rākṣasas and the vānaras.
t.6.81.8: Then those monkeys and rākṣasas struck one another in battle with variegated maces, with darts, swords and axes.
t.6.81.9: Rivers of blood began to flow, with elephants and chariots for their banks, horses for their fish and banners for their trees, bearing along rafts of bodies.
t.6.81.10: Leaping up again and again in the battle, the chiefs of the monkeys smashed banners, armour and chariots, horses, and weapons of various kinds.
t.6.81.11: With their sharp teeth and their nails as well, the monkeys tore away the hair, the ears, the foreheads and the noses of the rākṣasas.
t.6.81.12: In the battle, a hundred of the foremost vānaras rushed upon each and every rākṣasa, as birds rush upon a tree laden with fruit.
t.6.81.13: Likewise the mountain-like rākṣasas struck down the fierce vānaras with heavy maces, darts, swords and axes.
t.6.81.14: The great army of the vānaras, being slain by the rākṣasas, went for refuge to Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, who is the refuge of all.
t.6.81.15: Then the mighty Rāma of great splendour, taking up his bow, entered the Rākṣasa army and rained down a shower of arrows.
t.6.81.16: Then, as clouds in the sky cannot reach the sun, they could not approach Rāma, who had entered their midst, exceedingly terrible, burning them up with the fire of his arrows.
t.6.81.17: In the battle the night-roaming demons saw only the most terrible deeds done by Rāma, the feats of Rāma that were hard for anyone to accomplish.
t.6.81.18: They could not see Rāma as he shook the great army and scattered the great chariot-warriors, just as one cannot see the wind that has entered a forest.
t.6.81.19: They saw their army cut down, pierced and burned by arrows, shattered and afflicted by weapons at the hands of Rāma, but they did not see Rāma himself, so swiftly did he act.
t.6.81.20: They could not see Rāghava as he struck at their bodies, just as creatures cannot see the Self of all beings dwelling within the objects of the senses.
t.6.81.21: Here he strikes down the array of elephants, here he strikes down the great chariot-warriors, here with his sharp arrows he strikes down the foot-soldiers together with the horses.
t.6.81.22: Thus all those rākṣasas, enraged at one another, struck down in battle those who resembled Rāma; they did so because of their likeness to Rāghava.
t.6.81.23: Stupefied by the great-souled one with the supreme Gāndharva weapon, they could not see Rāma as he consumed the enemy host.
t.6.81.24: Those rākṣasas, however, saw thousands of Rāmas on the battlefield; and again they saw Kākutstha as one alone in that great battle.
t.6.81.25: They saw the golden tip of the great-souled one's bow whirling about like a circle of fire from a spinning firebrand, but they did not see Rāghava.
t.6.81.26: They beheld that wheel whose nave was his body, whose flame was his strength, whose spokes were his arrows, whose rim was his bow, whose roar was the twang of the bowstring and the slap of his palm, and whose radiance was his energy, intellect and virtues.
t.6.81.28: There was an army of ten thousand chariots swift as the wind, and eighteen thousand mighty, impetuous elephants.
t.6.81.27: Like the wheel of Time, that wheel of Rāma, its rim formed of divine missiles and the bowstring, was seen by all beings slaying the rākṣasas in battle.
t.6.81.29: There were fourteen thousand horses together with their riders, and a full two hundred thousand rākṣasas fighting on foot.
t.6.81.30: In the eighth part of the day, the hosts of the rākṣasas, who could take any form at will, were slain by Rāma alone with arrows like flames of fire.
t.6.81.31: Those night-rangers who were left of the slain, their horses killed, their chariots destroyed, their banners shattered, and themselves exhausted, fled back to the city of Laṅkā.
t.6.81.32: With its slain elephants, foot-soldiers and horses, that battlefield became like the playground of the enraged Rudra, the wielder of the Pināka bow.
t.6.81.33: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the supreme seers honored that deed of Rāma, crying, "Well done, well done!"
t.6.81.34: Then, immediately afterward, Rāma said to Sugrīva: “This divine power of weapons belongs either to me or to Tryambaka.”
t.6.81.35: Then, having slain that army of rākṣasas, the great-souled Rāma, equal to Śakra and one who had overcome weariness in the use of missiles and weapons, was praised by the delighted hosts of gods.
